Statement: The structure contains a complete, well-defined load path, including structural elements and connections, that serves to transfer the inertial forces associated with the mass of all elements of the building to the foundation.

The clear distance between the building being evaluated and any adjacent building is greater than 0.5% of the height of the shorter building in low seismicity, 1.0% in moderate seismicity, and 2.0% in high seismicity.

Interior mezzanine levels are braced independently from the main structure and are anchored to the seismic-force-resisting elements of the main structure with connections capable of developing the full capacity of the mezzanine framing.
The sum of the shear strengths of the seismic-force-resisting system in any story in each direction is not less than 90% of the strength in the adjacent story above.

The stiffness of the seismic-force-resisting system in any story is not less than 80% of the seismic-force-resisting system stiffness in an adjacent story above or less than 90% of the average seismic-force-resisting system stiffness of the three stories above.
All vertical elements in the seismic-force-resisting system are continuous to the foundation and have positive connection at all splices and connections.
There are no changes in the net horizontal dimension of the seismic-force-resisting system of more than 20% in a story relative to adjacent stories, excluding one-story penthouses and mezzanines.
There is no change in effective mass of more than 40% from one story to the next. Light roofs, penthouses, and mezzanines need not be considered.
The estimated distance between the story center of mass and the story center of rigidity is less than 15% of the building width in either plan dimension.

Liquefaction-susceptible, saturated, loose granular soils that could jeopardize the building's seismic performance do not exist in the foundation soils at depths within 75 ft (22.9 m) under the building. If present, the soils are stabilized or the foundation is designed to accommodate liquefaction effects.
The building site is located away from potential earthquake-induced slope failures or rockfalls, or the building is designed to accommodate the effects of such failures without damage.
Surface fault rupture and surface displacement at the building site are not anticipated (? or the building is designed to accommodate the effects of such displacement).
The ratio of the least horizontal dimension of the seismic-force-resisting system at the foundation level to the building height (base-height) is greater than 0.8Sa.
The foundation has ties capable of developing the full seismic force demands where footings, piles, and piers are not restrained by beams, slabs, or soils classified as Site Class A, B, or C.
The number of lines of shear walls in each principal direction is greater than or equal to 2.
The shear stress in the reinforced masonry shear walls, calculated using the Quick Check procedure of Section 4.4.3.3, is less than 70 lb/in² (0.48 MPa).

The shear stress in the unreinforced masonry shear walls, calculated using the Quick Check procedure of Section 4.4.3.3, is less than 30 lb/in² (0.21 MPa) for clay units and 70 lb/in² (0.48 MPa) for concrete units. Bays with openings greater than 25% of the wall area shall not be included in Aw of Eq. (4-8).
Masonry is in full contact with frame.
Diaphragms are connected for transfer of loads to the shear walls, and the connections are able to develop the lesser of the shear strength of the walls or diaphragms.

All concrete columns are doweled into the foundation with a minimum of four bars, and the dowels are able to develop the tensile capacity of reinforcement in columns of the seismic-force-resisting system.

Secondary components have the shear capacity to develop the flexural strength of the components and are Compliant with the following items: COLUMN-BAR SPLICES, BEAM-BAR SPLICES, COLUMN-TIE SPACING, STIRRUP SPACING, and STIRRUP AND TIE HOOKS.
Flat slabs or plates not part of the seismic-force-resisting system have continuous bottom steel through the column joints.
All wall openings that interrupt rebar have trim reinforcing on all sides.
The height-to-thickness ratio of the unreinforced infill walls at each story is less than 13.
The infill walls are not of cavity construction.
The infill walls are continuous to the soffits of the frame beams and to the columns to either side.
The diaphragms are not composed of split-level floors and do not have expansion joints.
Diaphragm openings immediately adjacent to the shear walls are less than 15% of the wall length.
Diaphragm openings immediately adjacent to exterior masonry shear walls are not greater than 4 ft long.
There is tensile capacity to develop the strength of the diaphragm at reentrant corners or other locations of plan irregularities.
There is reinforcing around all diaphragm openings larger than 50% of the building width in either major plan dimension.
Pile caps have top reinforcement, and piles are anchored to the pile caps; the pile cap reinforcement and pile anchorage are able to develop the tensile capacity of the piles.

Anchors of concrete or masonry walls to wood structural elements are installed taut and are stiff enough to limit the relative movement between the wall and the diaphragm to no greater than 1/8 in. before engagement of the anchors.
